purpose: Consolidate prior genuine action-description comparisons into a single master review surface; distinguish evidence-verified membership, proposed action equivalence, source dependence, rite ownership and publication authority.

methodology.family_clusters: 26 existing McLoughlin family action clusters; all 70 original observation IDs checked; all proposed owner/group IDs checked against 465-registry, not same custom certification.
methodology.description_pairs: 41 previously manually compared descriptions; verifies left source-action IDs against original three-books register; semantic findings are prior editorial review, not independently reverified original book facsimiles.
methodology.provisional_clusters: 12 existing regional/institutional clusters checked against all 465 known registry IDs, prevent same occasion/feast collapsing separate acts.

review_priority.same_core_or_variant_first: Compare actors, exact action, occasion, geography and actual textual dependence; same generic action can have separate local variants
review_priority.false_lexical_matches: Keep negative edges to prevent future bad automatic clustering
review_priority.rite_boundaries: Priest blessings, 1962 rites and lay customs must have distinct owner pointers
review_priority.region: Geographical overlap never establishes globally observed custom

description_pair_edges.left_action: Mark a family Paschal candle with five cloves in cross form
description_pair_edges.right_action: Insert five cloves into a home Paschal candle as a devotional image
description_pair_edges.reason: Both describe fitting five cloves into a family Paschal candle; source dependence and exact construction differ or remain unknown.

description_pair_edges.left_action: Give Easter eggs decorated in red or gold with Resurrection symbols
description_pair_edges.right_action: Easter eggs decorated with Resurrection symbols
description_pair_edges.reason: Both describe decorating Easter eggs with specifically Christian Resurrection symbols; color or application details vary.

description_pair_edges.left_action: Make an Easter Wreath of Victory from laurel and flowers
description_pair_edges.right_action: Christmas laurel wreath with victory symbolism

description_pair_edges.left_action: Renew baptismal vows together as a family at Easter dinner
description_pair_edges.right_action: Renew baptismal vows collectively before Easter
description_pair_edges.reason: Both report a family renewal of baptismal vows during the Easter period; one specifically places it at dinner and the other before Easter.

description_pair_edges.left_action: Renew baptismal vows together as a family at Easter dinner
description_pair_edges.right_action: Renew baptismal vows at the home altar on the baptism anniversary
description_pair_edges.reason: The Kelly rite is a baptism-anniversary family home-altar observance, rather than the fixed Easter family dinner renewal.

description_pair_edges.left_action: Paint Easter eggs with a victory banner or Chi-Rho emblem
description_pair_edges.right_action: Paint Easter eggs with crosses and other symbols of Christ's victory
description_pair_edges.reason: Painting Easter eggs with a Cross or Chi-Rho is a more specific variant of Christian victory motifs described in the earlier Mueller action.

description_pair_edges.left_action: Retain a lantern of fire from the Holy Saturday Vigil for household devotion
description_pair_edges.right_action: Taking home Easter Vigil blessed fire by lantern
description_pair_edges.reason: Both report carrying the newly blessed Easter fire away from the Vigil by lantern to the home; distinct source independence unverified.

description_pair_edges.left_action: Set a carved white dove above the Pentecost altar decorations
description_pair_edges.right_action: Pentecost altar decorated in red with dove
description_pair_edges.reason: Both describe a home Pentecost devotional altar including a dove, with the later source specifying a carved white image.

description_pair_edges.right_action: Arrange a paper tableau with dove seven gifts and cosmos symbols for Pentecost

description_pair_edges.right_action: Cleaning and decorating graves before All Souls
description_pair_edges.reason: All Souls cemetery visits with flowers and maintaining relatives' graves overlap cleaning/decorating graves, but visiting and tending are separable actions.

description_pair_edges.left_action: Add a handful of earth to a coffin after marking a cross over it
description_pair_edges.right_action: Louisiana funeral attendees cast earth on coffin
description_pair_edges.reason: Casting earth upon a coffin overlaps the reported Louisiana funeral action, but the first book's geographic context is different or incompletely resolved.

description_pair_edges.right_action: Slovak honeyed Christmas oblatky distributed
description_pair_edges.reason: Both describe Slovak Christmas oblatky distribution to families; the Family Life Bureau report specifies organists and one per household member.

description_pair_edges.right_action: Some families light central Christ candle each of twelve Christmas days

description_pair_edges.right_action: New Easter fire carried home in lantern
description_pair_edges.reason: An Easter fire carried home from a church Vigil is reported in both books, but the McLoughlin text has a material and devotional-specific context.

regional_or_institutional_cluster_cases.action_scope_reason: Local Seises dance at Corpus Christi and Immaculate Conception may belong to one Seville practice with separate occurrences; never two automatic global customs.
Priestly blessing of flower wreaths and keeping the blessed wreaths later are different stages of one regional object tradition; minister blessing not assumed lay-performable.
Priestly house blessing and Magi initials/chalking at the door may be linked seasonally but involve distinct ministerial and household practices.

Extinguishing household fires and bringing home the Easter Vigil blessed fire can form a single local sequence; confirm place and permitted transport instead of asserting two separate universal customs.
Marian-image relay, Saint Joseph image visits and Herbergsuchen lodging play share Advent hospitality themes but involve different image, roles and enactment; no combined automatic identity.
Candlemas candle blessing/decorating and All Souls family prayer with an already blessed candle occur on different dates with distinct actions.
All Souls family portions, bread alms, food charities and hospitality to orphaned children share charitable intention but are country/food/action variants; no single unqualified new custom.
Egg dyeing, coloured designs, gifts, rolling and hunts do not all describe the same action; retain related subtypes rather than indiscriminately merge.
Prayerful symbolism of Lenten pretzels and giving pretzels to the poor can be two uses of the same food with a distinct charity action.
Spanish Immaculate Conception novenas/processions and household balcony decoration share a feast but are distinct actions.
Blessing of graves by clergy, grave cleaning, lanterns and Brazilian/Philippine observances are not one homogeneous ritual; link selectively to cemetery visit existing owner.
Keeping the Christmas crib up until Candlemas is an optional local household custom, not a universal definition of liturgical Christmastide.
